principles: Public sources only. Nothing confidential, internal or personal is collected.
Original sources are preferred: the organisation that did the work or holds the evidence. A third-party report is used only when no original can be found, and is labelled as such.
UK government sources are checked first, then AI developers' own threat and safety reporting, then independent evaluators.

categories.name: UK government
categories.why: Authoritative UK assessments, guidance and legislation, and the UK's own testing of frontier AI.

sources.name: UK Parliament bill pages (Cyber Security and Resilience Bill)

categories.name: AI developer
categories.why: First-hand reporting of real misuse of their models, and of the cyber capability of new models before and at release.

sources.name: OpenAI threat reporting, system cards and deployment safety

categories.name: Independent evaluator
categories.why: Capability and behaviour evidence from organisations that test models but don't build them, and the shared catalogue of attacks on AI systems.

categories.name: Legal and policy analysis
categories.why: Explains regulatory changes (for example EU AI Act timelines) where the official text is hard to read or not yet published.

sources.name: Law firm and policy institute briefings, case by case

categories.name: News and model trackers
categories.why: Early warning of model releases and incidents. Always replaced by an original source when one is published.

sources.name: Model release trackers and reputable technology news, case by case
